If the display stays on while the tablet is asleep, which can drain a whole night, the guard starts after 2 minutes and keeps trying every few minutes until the display goes off. It tells the Boox sleep screen that the display is on, asks it to refresh, locks the screen, wakes the tablet and locks it again, and with Shizuku presses the wake and sleep keys. After each try the log says which step worked; none has been seen to work on this tablet yet, and Shizuku is only needed for the last.

On this tablet the display has stayed on, draining the battery overnight, exactly 90 minutes after the sleep screen last refreshed, each time after Android had restarted by itself. While the tablet sleeps, the keep-alive asks the sleep screen to refresh every 30 minutes if nothing else has, which costs well under 1 mAh a night. It is a precaution against that pattern, not a proven cure.
Sleep guard (experimental): %1$s, and the display went to sleep.
Sleep guard (experimental) tried, and the display stayed on.

Android restarted by itself and the tablet hasn’t been restarted since. Until it is, the tablet can’t sleep deeply and may use several times as much asleep, and after the last two restarts like this the display stayed on all night and the battery emptied. Restart the tablet (hold the power button, then Restart) before you leave it asleep.
